content: P1 withdrawn (one change): GaME's opacity prune deletes Gaussians of earlier sessions as published, instead of ending them (death_prune) and keeping them in the GPU model. Nothing else in the decision core changes (split rules c066077 stay). run.py adds a per-round GPU readout (allocated/reserved peak) and a clean stop when the reserved peak exceeds GPU_GUARD_GB (default 14.5 of 16.3 GB) - a run limit, not a model parameter.

final2 06a3092 (snapshot runs/update_layer_game_T1_20261006/code_06a3092, final_code_hash.txt); dev carries the same commit. Unit tests 17/17 (footprint, prior t_L, l2 new-site, t1 birth/extractor, evidence scenarios).

P1 (1a24c78) kept pruned earlier-session rows so 'the maps of their keyframes' times keep them'. The history readouts (objects4d, retention, accept history) read session_X/timeline.pkl, whose scenes are RENDERED at each snapshot time (game.py snapshot()/_render_scene: the scene list stores renders, not rows), so a row pruned later is still in every earlier snapshot. The layer reads elements() = rows alive now; ended rows never enter a decision (game.py:1356). The decided version 29d7f6e (prune deleting) passed the accept history check on real A->B->C and synthetic A->B. What P1 did change: the official tsdf export of session B renders A's stored keyframes at their times, so pruned A rows were still rendered there; without P1 those renders use the pruned model (= the decided version's readout, real B 92.42 / synthetic B 87.76).

Measured: ~237 B/row parameters, ~977 B/row training footprint (param+grad+2 Adam+label). Crashed run syn_row4i B (P1 on): 13.2 GB used at frame 2269 with ~3.0 M alive rows plus the P1-ended rows (real B had 711,299 = 28 % of the model; synthetic B not counted before the crash), failed at frame 3241 (3.11 M alive) with dmesg dxgkio_make_resident ENOMEM. Decided version (no P1), same synthetic B: 2.96 -> 3.16 M alive rows, ran to the end on this card; older no-P1 synthetic runs sampled by nvidia-smi peaked at 11.4 GB used (syn_row4v6.log.vram). Prediction for syn B with P1 off: alive rows 3.0-3.2 M -> 3.1 GB of training rows + the fixed part (~6.4 GB: rasterizer buffers, keyframes, label table, allocator cache) = ~9.5-11.5 GB reserved; guard 14.5 GB stops the run cleanly if that is wrong. The readout in the log will give the actual per-round peak (this is also the first direct measurement; earlier numbers are nvidia-smi samples).

RAM: checkpoint_a 11.4 GB loaded once; process RSS of earlier synthetic B runs stayed below the 45 GB WSL limit with no side job; nothing else runs (single GPU job, GPU.lock). Disk: 393 GB used of the 450 GB cap (D: 316 GB free); outputs: checkpoint_b ~12 GB + timeline.pkl + eval -> < 20 GB; the crashed run's partial session_b is overwritten by --resume from checkpoint_a (no new directory).

synthetic B only, resumed from syn_row4i/checkpoint_a (A is unaffected by P1: in the first session there is no earlier-session row, death_prune stays empty, so A under aa4424b == A under c066077; A is not rerun - user: 合成A还要跑么). Then eval_row.sh synthetic (A and B evaluated from both checkpoints, retention A->B, render readouts). Expected wall time: B ~70 min + eval ~20 min.

Synthetic B G1 F1 reference points: decided syn_row4s3cb 87.76 (no P1, lenient footprint), row 1 84.91, row 3 90.25; synthetic A (c066077, syn_row4i): 22 closures, 21 consistent with the GT motions. Expectation: B >= 87.76 (the split rules improved real C 93.80 -> 94.58 with the same core; P1 off returns the export to the decided readout). A reported as measured; no shrinking of conclusions, no repeat runs.

(1) GPU GUARD line in the log (reserved > 14.5 GB) -> run stops by itself, no eval, report the peak and the element count. (2) any CUDA/driver error -> no retry, record and report. (3) accept history FAIL or B closures inconsistent with GT_ANIMATION_INTERVALS -> stop before any real chain, analyse offline on the B checkpoint first. (4) B G1 < 87.76 -> report the number and the decomposition; no tuning, no further chain until the user decides.

Real ABC under the same core: real_row4i C 94.58/94.40/94.49 official, accept history PASS (lost 0), object F1 98.42; real_row4g A 93.22 / B 92.89 (P1 on). P1 off real evidence: decided 29d7f6e (prune deleting) real A 93.31 / B 92.42 / C 94.57, accept PASS - the prune mode alone never broke a history check. Element-rule and footprint verdict counts on real elements/frames: fp4_a (1 closure, element_rule 134,858 vs base 130,303) recorded in prerun_review_final_9b58938 and footprint_d278057 addenda.

Synthetic A->B under the decided core (no P1) completed on this card with 2.96-3.16 M rows (syn_row4s3cb.log); synthetic A under c066077 completed (2.88 M rows, 11.4 GB checkpoint) and its closures match the GT motions 21/22. The only synthetic failure mode seen (two crashes) is GPU residency, which this change addresses directly; it is a hypothesis until the readout confirms the peak - the guard makes the failure mode harmless either way.

On a guard stop or crash: keep syn_row4i/checkpoint_a, record the peak, do not rerun; next step would be measuring the fixed part offline (CPU-side count of keyframe/raster buffers) before any further GPU job. On metric failure: offline analysis on checkpoint_b (closure_compare, state_rows, g1_decompose) only.

If B passes the stop rules: real A->B->C with the same code 06a3092 (one chain, the deliverable), each session followed by eval; cleanup of superseded intermediates after each evaluation, newest checkpoints kept.
